anchor: regular wash of the sea against the hull
note: Wash: the gentle splash of waves.
A freshet is a flood in a stream from heavy rain or snowmelt.
Precipitous: very steep, like a cliff or mountain side.

anchor: some capricious revulsion of thought or feeling
note: Capricious: sudden, unpredictable. Revulsion: a sudden strong reaction.

anchor: a sullen revocation on the men’s part
note: Revocation: a taking back, a withdrawal of the cheer.
Strategic: planned to achieve an aim. The order to pipe down breaks up the crowd.

anchor: Shrill as the shriek of the sea-hawk
note: Sea-hawk: a large bird of prey that hunts over the sea.
Mechanism: a machine-like system working without thought.
Trimming the yards means turning the yards to catch the wind.
Ballasted: weighted, here with cannonballs to sink the body.
The sail-maker’s mates sewed the dead into hammocks for burial at sea.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Sail-maker”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

anchor: the tilted plank let slide its freight into the sea
note: A burial plank tilted so the body slid out under the flag.

anchor: the stridor or bony creak of their gaunt double-jointed pinions
note: Stridor: a harsh creaking noise. Pinions: wings.

anchor: the croaked requiem of their cries
note: A requiem is a mass or song for the dead.
Prodigy: a marvel. The calm of Billy’s hanging seemed supernatural.
Encroachment: the crowd began to push forward on the deck.
Beating to quarters called every man to his station for battle.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Beat to quarters”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

note: Peremptoriness: sharp demand for instant obedience.

anchor: superinduces in average man a sort of impulse of docility
note: Superinduces: adds on top of. Docility: readiness to obey.

anchor: sworded Lieutenants commanding the sections of batteries below
note: Each lieutenant led a section of guns on a gun deck.

anchor: Captain Vere, a martinet as some deemed him
note: A martinet is a strict disciplinarian who insists on every rule.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Martinet”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

anchor: the story of Orpheus with his lyre spellbinding the wild denizens of the wood
note: In Greek myth Orpheus played his lyre so sweetly that wild beasts and even trees followed him.

anchor: the disruption of forms going on across the Channel
note: Vere refers to the French Revolution’s overthrow of old customs.
A naval chaplain led daily prayers.
Circumambient: surrounding on all sides.
